holidays.name: National Homemade Cookie Day
holidays.description: A day to ditch the store-bought packages and get flour on your elbows. Bakers everywhere are encouraged to whip up a batch of chocolate chip, oatmeal raisin, or snickerdoodle cookies from scratch and share them with anyone who comes near the kitchen.
holidays.origin: An unofficial American food holiday that spread through food-industry calendars and social media, celebrating the tradition of baking cookies at home.
holidays.funFact: The word 'cookie' comes from the Dutch 'koekje,' meaning 'little cake,' and early cookies were reportedly made as test pieces to check oven temperature before baking cakes.

holidays.name: International Coffee Day
holidays.description: A global caffeine-fueled celebration of the beloved bean. Cafes hand out free or discounted cups while coffee lovers toast the drink that powers mornings, deadlines, and questionable all-nighters.
holidays.origin: Officially launched by the International Coffee Organization in 2015 in Milan, Italy, though various countries had marked coffee days on this date earlier.
holidays.funFact: Legend says coffee was discovered by an Ethiopian goat herder named Kaldi, who noticed his goats dancing around after eating berries from a certain tree.

holidays.name: World Vegetarian Day
holidays.description: A day to promote the joys of plant-based eating and kick off Vegetarian Awareness Month. Cooks are invited to give meatless meals a try and discover that a veggie plate can be thrilling.
holidays.origin: Established in 1977 by the North American Vegetarian Society and endorsed by the International Vegetarian Union in 1978.
holidays.funFact: The word 'vegetarian' is often credited to the founding of the British Vegetarian Society in 1847, and it has nothing to do with the word 'vegetable' being a root, despite how it sounds.

holidays.name: International Day of Older Persons
holidays.description: A day to honor the wisdom, stories, and sass of older generations. It encourages people to call grandparents, listen to a few tall tales, and appreciate the folks who invented 'back in my day.'
holidays.origin: Designated by the United Nations General Assembly in 1990, first observed on October 1, 1991.
holidays.funFact: Japan has more than 90,000 centenarians, the highest per capita rate in the world, and it even has its own national holiday, Respect for the Aged Day.

holidays.name: Nikola Tesla-Style Oktoberfest Finale? No: Oktoberfest's Final Stretch
holidays.description: While the main Oktoberfest party in Munich wraps up in early October, this date lands in its last days, when beer tents hum with oompah bands, pretzels the size of dinner plates, and strangers swaying arm in arm.
holidays.origin: Oktoberfest began in 1810 as a celebration of the marriage of Crown Prince Ludwig of Bavaria to Princess Therese, and it has since evolved into the world's largest folk festival.
holidays.funFact: Despite its name, most of Oktoberfest takes place in September, because the weather in Munich is warmer then.
